profile.legal_name: Holding Company of The Villages, Inc.
markets: The Villages, Central Florida (Sumter, Lake and Marion counties)
profile.org_note: One family-owned master developer, not a divisional builder: there are no regions or division presidents. The Morse family (siblings Mark Morse, Tracy Morse and Jennifer Parr) owns a holding company whose affiliates hold the land and build the homes (public records name The Villages Land Company, LLC, The Villages Development Company, The Villages of Lake-Sumter, Inc. and Buffalo Hide and Cattle Company). Land and capital decisions sit with the family and the CEO, Robert Chandler IV, who ran development before his 2026 promotion; Martin Dzuro handles entitlements. No CFO or treasurer is publicly named.
profile.summary: Not a conventional production homebuilder: The Villages is a single, family-owned, age-restricted (55+) master-planned retirement community in Central Florida that develops its own land and builds and sells its own homes (about 83,400 units sold to date, more than 2,100 in 2026 through mid-October, average price just under $500,000, per an October 2026 bond roadshow reported by Bloomberg). The community covers about 57,000 acres, the family holds tens of thousands of undeveloped acres around it, and roads, utilities, golf and recreation are paid for by its community development districts selling tax-exempt special assessment bonds that homebuyers repay. It is an unlikely land-banking customer: it owns decades of land outright, does not buy finished lots from third parties, and already has cheap, non-recourse lot-development money through district bonds.

people.name: Robert Chandler IV
people.title: CEO
people.prior_role: Vice President of Development, The Villages (2023 to 2026, succeeded Gary Moyer); joined The Villages in 2018 from Lake County government, where he was director of the Economic Growth Department
people.source_title: The Villages news post: AdventHealth to Anchor New Legacy Place With Hospital (quote attributed to 'Robert Chandler IV, CEO The Villages')
people.note: First non-family CEO. Appointment reported by Villages-News on 2026-01-17 (no effective date given); background and prior titles are from that report (https://www.villages-news.com/2026/01/17/first-non-family-member-to-serve-as-ceo-of-the-villages/). He ran development (land entitlement and build-out) before becoming CEO, so he is both the top executive and the most senior known land decision-maker. Reporting line to the Morse family owners is inferred: the report says Mark Morse stated he is 'not going anywhere'. The 2026 Builder 100 listing still shows Mark Morse as CEO, which appears out of date.

people.name: Mark Morse
people.title: Owner
people.prior_role: CEO of The Villages from 2014 (after the death of his father, H. Gary Morse); described in Feb 2024 as CEO of The Villages Development Company and Buffalo Hide and Cattle Company, the family land-holding entities
people.source_title: Villages-News: First non-family member to serve as CEO of The Villages
people.note: Current formal title is not published. Villages-News reports it is unclear how much control he has handed over. Florida Trend (2024-02-12, https://floridatrend.com/article/39191/endless-horizon) reported he and his two sisters each received a one-third share of the company in 2006. Land purchases have historically been made through family entities he led, so treat him as a land and capital decision-maker until shown otherwise. Title note: Morse family; former CEO, succeeded by Robert Chandler IV in 2026.

people.name: Martin L. Dzuro
people.title: Senior Vice President of Development
people.source_title: Villages-News: Top official with The Villages submits Monarch Ranch annexation application
people.note: Goes by Marty. Title 'senior vice president of development' is from a 2023-08-02 Villages-News report (https://www.villages-news.com/2023/08/02/morse-family-and-the-villages-top-brass-pony-up-contributions-for-desantis-white-house-bid/); 2025 reports confirm he is still acting for The Villages on land matters but give no title: he filed the Wildwood annexation application for part of Monarch Ranch (May 2025) and presented the Coleman Ridge plan to the Sumter County Commission (Jan 2025, https://www.villages-news.com/2025/01/28/village-of-fenney-residents-wary-about-massive-coleman-ridge-development/). Best public candidate for the day-to-day land entitlement and development contact. Current title not confirmed after the 2026 CEO change. Title note: Title as published Aug 2023.

people.name: Jennifer Parr
people.title: Vice President
people.source_title: Villages-News: First non-family member to serve as CEO of The Villages
people.note: Daughter of H. Gary Morse and sister of Mark Morse; co-owner (one-third share transferred in 2006 per Florida Trend). Florida Trend (2024-02-12) gave her title as Sales and Marketing Vice President.

people.name: Tracy Morse
people.title: Co-owner
people.source_title: Villages-News: The Villages selling off Citizens First Bank
people.note: Sister of Mark Morse and Jennifer Parr; named as one of H. Gary Morse's three children who inherited the family businesses. Florida Trend (2024-02-12) names her as Tracy Mathews, holder of a one-third share since 2006, and an older report said she oversaw design. Her daughter Lindsey Blaise ran the family's Citizens First Bank until 2024. A September 2025 Villages-News report styles her Tracy Morse Dadeo (https://www.villages-news.com/2025/09/13/unitedhealthcare-wants-to-ask-morse-family-where-the-money-went/). Title note: Morse family; no operating title published.
